component.name: Scan to PDF
component.summary: Scan documents from a network scanner into PDF files

description.p: Scan to PDF scans every sheet in your scanner's document feeder, one- or two-sided, and saves the pages as one PDF. It talks directly to network scanners that support WSD (Web Services on Devices), such as the Epson ES-580W; no scanner driver is needed.

ul.li: Lossless scans when JPEG compression is not good enough
Brightness and contrast, where the scanner supports them
Only offers the settings your scanner supports
Optional text recognition (OCR) with OCRmyPDF or Tesseract
Page preview; remove single pages before saving
Status bar icon and start at login
Shares its settings with the wsdscan command-line tool

screenshot.caption: After a scan, with text recognition

description.p: Security hardening: device addresses are pinned to the answering host, only HTTP(S) without redirects or proxies, limits for responses, pages and images, robust image parsing, device texts cleaned, files written without following symlinks, safer installer and autostart entry.

Fixes: texts with “&” (e.g. “Black & white”) were not shown; page previews no longer depend on optional gdk-pixbuf loaders; switching scanners in the main window could crash and could lose settings the previous scanner did not offer. Folders in the home folder are shown as “~/…”. Screenshots added.

Every scanner has its own settings and its own page in the preferences, with an editable name (the device name is proposed), Duplicate and Remove. The main window and the preferences use the same scanner names.
Several scanners: add, edit and remove them in the preferences, choose a default, and switch between them in the main window.
Status bar icon and start at login; page preview with an optional review step to remove pages; text recognition (OCR) with OCRmyPDF or Tesseract.
